_comment: Settings for the AI ensemble pattern products (scripts/ai_ensemble_*.py; docs/ai_ensembles/README.md). Open AI ensembles (ECMWF AIFS ENS, NOAA AIGEFS) with physics baselines (ECMWF IFS ENS, NOAA GEFS), cut to the West, plus a calibration against satellite large-fire growth days. The local products are not published; the interactive research viewer is (web_publish), framed as experimental research from public data (analyst, 2026-10-10). Paths are relative to the repo root.
_comment_enabled: enabled: whether the scheduled daily run (scripts/ai_ensemble_daily.py) does anything; --force runs anyway.
_comment_dirs: data_dir: fetched runs, climatology and the calibration history. output_dir: one folder per products run, latest/ (newest complete set) and logs/.
_comment_task: Daily task start (local time; scripts/setup_ai_ensemble_task.ps1). All four 00Z runs are posted by ~01:00 PDT; AIGEFS takes ~1 h from NOMADS, so 02:30 has products ready ~03:45, well before 06:00. The 06Z runs don't finish until after 05:00, so a run started then always uses 00Z.
_comment_keep: keep_output_runs: dated products folders kept in output_dir (latest/ is separate). keep_cycles: fetched runs kept per model in data_dir/runs/ (~75-130 MB each).
_comment_web: web_export: build the interactive research viewer (<output_dir>/web/, scripts/ai_ensemble_web_export.py) on every daily run. web_publish: also push it to GitHub Pages (config/github_pages_config.json's ai_ensemble_clone_path, e.g. bah7-humboldt.github.io/ca-ai-ensemble-research); each push replaces the repo history so it holds one day. Public page, framed as experimental research from public data (analyst 2026-10-10); only the openly licensed models are ever exported. web_publish false since 2026-10-28: the site is built and deployed by the GitHub Actions cloud run (docs/ai_ensembles/README.md, Cloud run); turning it back on would push to main of the pipeline repo.
_comment_pyroconvection_page: pyroconvection_page: add the research viewer's guide/pyroconvection.html (pyroCb / pyroCu days of seven California fires against this project's 500 hPa regimes and documented patterns, the PFT ingredient thresholds, soundings) plus a pyroconvection line on each regime page. Reads <data_dir>/history/calibration/pyroconv/ (exported by scripts/pyrocb_patterns.py). Added 2026-10-17; turned on 2026-10-17 after the analyst reviewed the local preview (the viewer is public).
_comment_extra_fields: extra_fields: per-model fields beyond 'fields' (added 2026-10-11): 700 hPa temperature + humidity (700 hPa dryness), 2 m temperature + dewpoint / RH (surface RH), CAPE where published. AIGEFS has no surface humidity and no CAPE; AIFS has no CAPE. u10/v10: 10 m wind, for the footprint Hot-Dry-Windy analogue.

weathernext3.label: Google WeatherNext 3 (AI)
weathernext3._note: Google DeepMind access requested 2026-10-10 (GCS Zarr). Experimental terms; stub in ai_ensemble_sources.py.

_gradients_note: MSLP difference first minus second, hPa; offshore = negative. Thresholds are STARTING POINTS to calibrate against past events, not established criteria.

gradients.name: SAC-MFR
gradients._comment: North-wind gradient (2026-10-13): Sacramento minus Medford, after the NWS Redding north-wind technique (MFR -> RBL -> SAC gradient) in 'Critical Fire Weather Patterns of the United States'. Negative = higher pressure at Medford (northerly). Top 2 % of MFR-SAC ran x2.7 for >= 1,000-ac Sacramento Valley / Northwestern Mountains growth days, 2001-2025.
gradients.label: Sacramento minus Medford (north wind)

_wind850_note: 850 hPa wind blowing FROM a direction inside dir_from (degrees, clockwise) at or above min_kt counts as offshore. Starting points to calibrate.
_comment_rh_stations: rh_stations: ASOS sites whose fire-day minimum RH (and strongest wind/gust) are calibrated as surface-dryness predictors (added 2026-10-11). The forecast side reads the models' 2 m temperature + dewpoint (RH for GEFS) at the nearest 0.5 deg cell; AIGEFS has no surface humidity. Each belongs to the footprint listed in 'footprints'.
_comment_footprints: footprints: the PSAs each measure is scored against (analyst 2026-10-10: "the patterns need to match the actual growth footprint from the satellite detections"). A measure's large-growth days are counted from satellite growth inside its footprint's PSAs only, not the whole GACC. 'members' lists the gradient names (A-B) and sounding sites (OAK...) that use it; region-mean measures use their whole GACC. Each has >= 30 days of >= 5,000 ac in its offshore season (checked 2026-10-10).

diablo.label: Bay Area, North Bay and Sacramento Valley foothills (Diablo / North wind)

northwind.label: Sacramento Valley, its foothills and the Northwestern Mountains (north wind)

far_north.label: North Coast, Northwestern Mountains and Northeast California

east_side.label: Northeast California, Northern Sierra and Far Eastside

santa_ana.label: Central and South Coast and the Southern California mountains (Santa Ana)

central_coast.label: Central Coast, Central Coast Interior and South Coast

san_diego.label: South Coast and the Eastern and Southern Mountains

_comment_natural_earth_dir: Natural Earth 50m country/state lines for the maps -- the copy the Rx window tool caches. Missing files just leave the lines off.
_comment_lightning_src: Vaisala NLDN strike exports ({ONCC,OSCC}/*.csv), read by ai_ensemble_history_lightning.py. LICENSE: raw strikes are never redistributed or offered for download; derived counts and heat maps may be published.
_comment_lightning_lopez: Lightning formula layer (ai_ensemble_lightning_lopez.py, added 2026-10-22): the ECMWF IFS lightning parameterization's shape (Lopez 2016) on IFS ENS open-data fields, calibrated to NLDN. enabled: fetch it in the daily run (~3.9 GB of byte ranges, ~5 min) and show it on the research viewer. max_lead_h: last IFS ENS step fetched (180 = seven fire days). Needs calibration/lightning_lopez.json (ai_ensemble_lightning_lopez_calibrate.py).

hawaii._comment: Hawaii (2026-10-13, analyst: 'California and Hawaii for focus'). Island groups as footprints (config/hawaii_psa/HAWAII_PSA.shp, ai_ensemble_history_hawaii.py). Station gradients along the chain; the trade-wind north-south gradient comes from ERA5 / the models.

_comment_domain_hawaii: lat_min 20 -> 15 on 2026-10-13 so the whole of Hawaii Island (18.9 N) and the trade-wind gradient south of the chain are in the grid.

sundowner._comment: Sundowner gradient, Santa Maria minus Santa Barbara (DRI CEFA). Used by ai_ensemble_cefa_patterns.py (evening max); not a calibrated outlook row -- AUC 0.53 against Santa Barbara-area growth, 2001-2025. Its sign is the opposite of the offshore gradients, so it isn't in 'gradients' (those are scored by their minimum).

_comment_keep_cycles: Full runs kept per model in <data_dir>/runs/ (about 0.8 GB per day for all four). 4 since 2026-10-14 so the research viewer's run selector can show today plus the previous three daily runs.
